scope: W-20 Root mounts open FIFOs, sockets and devices as PHP 8.5.12 does, with waits bounded by the OpenFile context; local evidence only, no VM.

environment.containers: docker run --rm --network none --read-only, tmpfs work directory, probe scripts and test binaries mounted read-only

decisions: Policy.OpenFile takes a context first; it bounds the open and every later wait on the returned file. Decided by the implementing agent after an independent Fable 5.1 consultation, under the owner's 2026-11-07 rule that PHP-visible behaviour matches PHP 8.5.12 and internals use the best Go design.
Adopted from the consultation: wrapper errors name the PHP path; one private epoll per FIFO wait on Linux.

Root opens every device node as PHP does instead of the five-device allowlist the consultation suggested keeping: approved by the project owner on 2026-11-07. Capability, identity, hard-link and OS permission checks stay in force, and FileGrant.Root documents that every node under the mount is reachable.
O_RDONLY with O_CREAT or O_TRUNC on a directory reports EISDIR, following Linux open(2); macOS would open the directory for O_CREAT. PHP fopen modes never use these combinations.

commands.command: tests/policy/special-files/probe.sh in the arm64, amd64 and i386 images (read-only, no network, tmpfs work directory)
commands.result: Same semantics on all three images (amd64.log, i386.log differ only in emulated start-up time). fopen(FIFO,'r') returns when a writer opens, before it writes; w/a/c wait for a reader; r+ returns at once; x reports File exists; EPIPE gives a Notice; include FIFO waits, then warns 'Failed to open stream: Success'; /dev/tty and sockets fail with 'No such device or address'; directories opened for writing fail with 'Is a directory'.

commands.command: php/devices-linux.sh with a dev tmpfs and the loop-device cgroup rule (arm64)
commands.result: A relocated null device and a loop block device open and read; a device outside the cgroup reports 'Operation not permitted'; php and include on a FIFO without a writer wait (timeout exit 124).

commands.command: Go syscall probes of FIFO and pty readiness (go-probe/*.go.txt) on darwin/arm64 and in the linux/arm64 image
commands.result: Both kernels: nonblocking read returns 0 with no writer and EAGAIN with an idle writer; Linux reports a writer that left as EPOLLHUP, macOS reports nothing. Linux FIFOs and both kernels' ptmx accept deadlines; darwin FIFOs do not.

commands.command: go test of the new policy regressions on a3dd3ac's internal/policy (the call helper adapted to the old OpenFile signature)
commands.result: Every new regression fails before the change; TestRootAllowsCharacterDevices and TestRootFIFOSwapStaysBounded are invariants and pass. red-policy-linux-arm64.log repeats this in the linux/arm64 image, where TestRootFIFOReadSeesWriterThatLeft also runs and fails.

commands.command: go test of the RunFile regressions on 7b82315 sources
commands.result: TestRunFileFIFORunsWriterSource, TestRunFileFIFOCancelReleasesAdmission, TestRunFileSocketFailsLikeKernel and TestRunFileReadsDevicesLikePHP fail before the change on darwin and in the linux/arm64 image (red-runfile-linux-arm64.log).

commands.command: go test -overlay with the wrapper's PHP-path rewrite removed
commands.result: EPIPE and ESPIPE errors carried the host temporary directory before the rewrite.

commands.command: go test -overlay with the alias checks moved back after the open
commands.result: TestRootRefusedFIFOAliasIsNotOpened fails: the refused open released the waiting FIFO writer.

commands.command: CGO_ENABLED=0 cross-compiled policy and root test binaries run in the arm64, amd64 and i386 images
commands.result: All tests pass on the three Linux kernels; only the two existing case-insensitive-volume tests skip.

commands.command: .github/workflows/special-files.yml run 42365853229 on a059e00, macOS 15 arm64: locked PHP 8.5.12 built from source, probe.sh, then go test -run 'TestRoot|TestRunFile' ./internal/policy .
commands.result: PHP's FIFO semantics match the Linux images, including fopen returning when a writer opens and closes without data; only libc message texts differ (Device not configured, Operation not supported on socket, Undefined error: 0). Phego's tests pass on the runner (ci/macos-15/phego-tests.log); TestRootFIFOReadSeesWriterThatLeft skips, the recorded macOS limit.

commands.command: the same job on macOS 15 Intel
commands.result: Identical to arm64 apart from temporary paths; Phego's tests pass (ci/macos-15-intel/phego-tests.log).

commands.command: the same run on Windows Server 2025: official php-8.5.12-1-nts-Win32-vs17-x64.zip, probe-windows.ps1, then TestWindowsSpecialFileReport
commands.result: PHP opens bare NUL, but <dir>\NUL, CON, COM1 and CONIN$ report 'No such file or directory', and directories opened with r, w, r+ or a report 'Permission denied'. Root refuses the reserved names as outside-root, opens a directory read-only and reports 'is a directory' for write modes (ci/windows-2025/phego-report.log): recorded in W-20.md as a follow-up.

commands.command: GitHub checks of PR #136 at a059e00
commands.result: All 47 checks succeed, including Go checks (ubuntu go test, race, vet), the Linux reference workflows and the new macOS and Windows jobs.

commands.command: CGO_ENABLED=0 cross-compiled policy and root test binaries at a059e00 run in the arm64, amd64 and i386 images
commands.result: Every test passes on the three Linux kernels; only the two existing case-insensitive-volume tests skip.

commands.command: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./... for the host and linux/386, windows/amd64, darwin/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/arm64, freebsd/amd64
go vet ./... for the host and linux/amd64, linux/386, windows/amd64, freebsd/amd64
commands.result: No findings except linux/386: internal/runtime/execution_output_bench_test.go:25 uses 1 << 40 as an int, which overflows on 32-bit. That file comes from main (81f9ac8) and this change does not touch internal/runtime; CI vets only the host platform.
Every package passes without race reports.

limits: A FIFO open returns up to about 10 ms after its peer arrives: the kernel gives no event when a writer connects without writing, so the open probes between pauses.
On macOS and the BSDs a writer that opens and closes a FIFO without writing between two probes is not seen; the open keeps waiting for a writer or the context.
Reads of regular files and directories, and calls into a trusted fs.FS, are not interrupted by the context.
PHP's include and fopen messages for these files are produced by W-17 and W-18 from OpenFile's result; no PHP code runs here yet.

Windows: os.Root refuses reserved device names under a mount (PHP reports them as missing files) and directories open differently from PHP ('Permission denied' in PHP); follow-up work, outside the FIFO and device waits.
linux/386 go vet fails on internal/runtime/execution_output_bench_test.go from main, independent of this change.
